run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T13:33:12Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend coincides with an ~8-minute outage of its ad dependency caused by a rolling restart of Deployment otel-demo/ad at 13:32:01Z. Frontend's error spans are confined to operations GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data and the client operation grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, with identical per-point error counts, and they run from about 13:32 to 13:40. Ad's own server-side GetAds span activity vanished from roughly 13:33 to 13:41, its new pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was marked Ready at 13:32:04 (its template has no readiness probe) although its only log line, 'Ad service starting.', appears at 13:36:14, and that new pod was CPU-throttled in 99-100% of CFS periods from 13:33:12 to 13:38:12 with usage pinned at its 50m limit. The restart is a controller rollout (SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete, restartCount 0, annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:32:01Z), not damage. Supported hypothesis: the single-replica ad Deployment was restarted, its new pod was considered Ready before the throttled JVM could serve, the old pod was deleted at 13:32:04, so frontend's GetAds calls errored and the frontend request error signal rose. The exact alert expression and the reported 2.3555 value could not be reproduced because no alerting rules are loaded in this Prometheus.

claims.text: Frontend error spans: increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]) was 0 at 13:32:12Z, first non-zero (150) at 13:33:12Z, peaked at 1015.5555555555555 at 13:37:12Z, was 208.88888888888889 at 13:43:12Z and 0 again at 13:44:12Z, so frontend error-span activity ran roughly 13:32-13:40Z.

At the alert start instant 2026-11-16T13:33:12Z, sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) was 0.5 error spans/s, and the GET operation error ratio was 1.4780600461893765% (GET error-span rate 0.11851851851851852/s vs GET UNSET 7.9/s).

Frontend's error spans by span_name were carried only by GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (identical per-point values, e.g. 96.496125, 228.88888888888889, 246.66666666666669, 229.19484047619048, 117.77777777777779) and tcp.connect; all other frontend span names (GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/*, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, executing api route pages /api/cart and /api/checkout) had zero error increase.

Kubernetes events show an ad Deployment rollout at 13:32:01-13:32:04Z: ScalingReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 0->1 and SuccessfulCreate of pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz at 13:32:01Z (Scheduled, Pulled 'already present', Created, Started 13:32:02-13:32:03Z), then ScalingReplicaSet ad-554b849958 1->0, Killing of pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq ('Stopping container ad') and SuccessfulDelete at 13:32:04Z.

The new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 pod template carries the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:32:01Z; apart from that annotation its template is identical to the superseded ad-554b849958 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, same env including AD_PORT=8080, same resources, no readinessProbe).

Deployment otel-demo/ad has spec.replicas=1, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25%, container ad has no readinessProbe (probes null), resources.limits.cpu=50m / memory 450Mi, and the Deployment carries deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2.

Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was created at 13:32:01Z, its ad container started at 13:32:03Z, its Ready condition became True at 13:32:04Z (no readiness probe in the template), restartCount is 0 and lastState is empty.

The only log line readable from pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz in 13:00-13:54Z is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-16T13:36:14.903167388Z, i.e. about 4 minutes after the container started at 13:32:03Z; no error lines were present.

Ad service span activity disappeared during the rollout: sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="ad"}[1m])) was 120 at 13:33:00Z, then 0 at every 15s step from 13:33:15Z through 13:40:45Z, and non-zero again (248) at 13:41:45Z; the GetAds server span increase was 38.666666666666664 at 13:34:00Z and 0 at 13:34:30Z, with ad's getAdsByCategory/getRandomAds/oteldemo.AdService/GetAds increases also 0 at 13:38:12Z and 13:40:12Z before recovering at 13:42:12Z.

The new ad pod was severely CPU-throttled: container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total/container_cpu_cfs_periods_total for pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was 0.9926984597317391 at 13:33:12Z, 0.997-1.0 from 13:34:12Z to 13:38:12Z, 0.9612220916568741 at 13:39:12Z and 0.7307110438729199 at 13:41:12Z, while its CPU usage was pinned at 0.0487-0.0496 cores from 13:34:12Z to 13:38:12Z (limit 0.05 cores / 50m). The previous pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq ran at ~0.004-0.02 cores with 4-20% throttling.

frontend-proxy's own error spans mirror the frontend route errors in the same minutes: span_name 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' had increases 97.56830416666666/228.88888888888889/248.8888888888889/229.19484047619048/134.44444444444446/20 at 13:34:12-13:44:12Z steps, against 0-6.7 before 13:32.

Among other services, only accounting and payment returned an error-span series and both stayed at 0 for the whole window; ad, fraud-detection and recommendation had only tiny increases (about 1.1111111111111112 per 5m), while cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote and shipping returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series at all (unknown, not zero).

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-vzsmb restarted after an OOM: its ad-independent container lastState.terminated reason is OOMKilled with exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-16T13:04:56Z, and it has been ready since 13:04:56Z with restartCount 1 - 27 minutes before the frontend error burst.

In the current pod list only ad's pod is young (ad-d89765fb5-whfnz, started 13:32:01Z, 0 restarts); all other otel-demo application pods, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6, started 12:59-13:01Z, and fraud-detection shows restartCount 1.

All 21 otel-demo Deployments, including ad and frontend, currently report replicas 1, ready 1 and available 1 with the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad / 2.1.3-frontend, i.e. the ad Deployment has recovered by the time of the query.

Likely cause chain: the restart of Deployment ad at 13:32:01Z replaced its only replica; because the container has no readiness/startup probe the new pod was declared Ready at 13:32:04 while the JVM was still CPU-throttled and not listening, the old pod was deleted at 13:32:04, ad served no GetAds spans from about 13:33 to 13:41, frontend's client operation grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds produced error spans (identical counts to its GET /api/data route and GET server-span errors, and mirrored by frontend-proxy 'ingress'/'router frontend egress' errors), and that error signal is what the RequestErrorRate alert on frontend reports. Parent-child call edges are not asserted because no span parent references were available.

The 50m CPU limit on the ad container is the main reason the restarted pod took so long to serve: its throttled-period ratio was essentially 1.0 and its usage was pinned at the 0.05-core limit from 13:33:12Z to 13:38:12Z while its first log line 'Ad service starting.' appeared only at 13:36:14Z and serving resumed around 13:41Z; without CPU throttling metrics per phase the attribution of the whole ~8-minute gap to throttling cannot be proven.

Ad did not crash or get OOMKilled/Evicted during the incident: the new pod's restartCount is 0, lastState is empty, no OOMKilled or Evicted event appears for ad pods (only Normal ScalingReplicaSet/Killing/SuccessfulDelete/Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started), and its only log line is the normal 'Ad service starting.' without any error text.

Ad's own error spans are not the driver of the frontend burst: ad's only error-span series in the window were flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at 1.1111111111111112 per 5m between 13:27:12Z and 13:31:12Z, before the frontend errors began, and ad's GetAds/getAdsByCategory/getRandomAds spans were recorded with STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no error) whenever they existed.

The fraud-detection OOMKill/restart at 13:04:56Z is not the cause of the frontend RequestErrorRate alert: it happened 27 minutes before the frontend error burst, the pod has been ready since 13:04:56Z, and fraud-detection's own error-span increase stayed at about 1.1111111111111112 per 5m against frontend's burst of up to 1015.5555555555555 per 5m.

Frontend's own pod was not replaced or restarted in the window: frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 started 12:59:34Z with restartCount 0, and the events query for involved objects matching ad- or frontend- returned only ad objects, while all Deployments are currently 1/1 ready.

Add a readinessProbe (and preferably a startupProbe) on gRPC port 8080 of the ad container, set the rolling update to maxUnavailable 0 (and/or run 2 replicas), and raise the 50m CPU limit so a restarted ad pod only receives Service traffic once it can actually serve.

Review who/what issued the ad Deployment restart at 2026-11-16T13:32:01Z (kubectl rollout restart is recorded only as the restartedAt annotation) and avoid restarting this single-replica latency-critical dependency during traffic peaks without a ready-gated rollout.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not loaded in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with type=alert returned no rules, evidence 5bbde812-9edc-4408-a3a7-cb6f65ba3ffa-t0:29c52e69-1494-4932-80e3-915c3b00195b, status no_data), so its exact expression and the annotation value 2.355555555555555 could not be verified or reproduced; my candidate GET error ratio at 13:33:12Z was 1.478%.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who or what triggered the ad rollout restart (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:32:01Z) is unknown.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend or ad in the incident window (0d2f6148-aea4-4424-97d1-6ea0f176496e-t0:4c2a0966-1c1a-43a7-bd35-016a5c80c7d4, 5bbde812-9edc-4408-a3a7-cb6f65ba3ffa-t3:f5a7c539-6d5d-4ed3-be1d-f4b55c771f5d, 75c3b5ba-d283-4c58-9171-5dfa7f2ed7db-t1:6ece5f9f-77bd-4afb-ad5f-f316d894369b), so span parent references, gateway error messages and the exact failed gRPC status code are unknown.

Frontend container logs returned no lines at all for 13:25-13:50Z (439ea754-65cd-489c-a26a-9bd7a0c959c2-t0:93868576-31a2-4249-8c57-5812007d591f, status no_data, 0 bytes), so frontend-side error messages could not be read.

kube-state-metrics series were unavailable in this view (kube_pod_container_info and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned no data, e.g. 209ccf59-ee02-4c72-b7e3-e8eb0cd6b722-t2:237fce5d-cf8d-4628-892f-4c437e6a25e8 and 45feb661-d78b-471b-91a1-55959afd2aac-t1:982deaf5-654e-45dc-ad8a-b0f4199bfeff), so the ad replica/ready timeline and the old pod's image digest could not be charted or compared.

The coarse 1m/2m scrape resolution leaves the exact instants of ad's serving stop (about 13:32:00-13:33:00Z) and resume (about 13:40:30-13:41:45Z) uncertain, and there is no evidence explaining what the ad process did between container start 13:32:03Z and its single log line at 13:36:14Z beyond CPU throttling.

For cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote and shipping no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series existed in the window, so their error state is unknown rather than zero, and no latency baseline comparison was available to test for a latency trend.
next_steps: Add a gRPC/TCP readinessProbe and startupProbe to the ad container and change the ad Deployment rollout to maxUnavailable: 0 (or 2 replicas) so the sole pod is not removed before the replacement can serve.
Consider raising the ad container CPU limit above 50m; measure ad startup time under the new limit before relying on it.
Trace the origin of the 2026-11-16T13:32:01Z kubectl rollout restart of deployment/ad via cluster audit logs or CI/CD records, which are not available in this Run.
Separately review the fraud-detection OOMKill (exitCode 137 at 13:04:56Z) and its memory limit, since it is an unrelated finding that did not cause this alert.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then.
